overview: Deere grew fiscal Q3 2026 net sales and revenues 5% to $12.608B and earned $1.379B, or $5.10 per share, as construction and forestry sales rose 18% and production and precision ag fell 6%. Deere raised FY2026 net income guidance to $4.75B-$5B, and Deanna Kovar, President of Worldwide Agriculture & Turf, called 2026 the ag cycle bottom with a measured 2027 recovery.
keyTakeaways: North American planter and sprayer early order programs are up mid-single digits versus last year's completed program, with See & Spray factory adoption nearly doubling.
Brent Norwood, CFO, said net tariffs will be a 2027 headwind, with the run rate near $1B versus about $750M net this year.
Chris Seibert, Director of Investor Relations, said C&F orders cover four to five months versus a typical two to three, on infrastructure, data centers and rental fleets.
Deere lowered its South America ag industry outlook to down 15%-20% and Europe to about flat.
financialHighlights: Equipment operations net sales rose 6% to $10.999B with a 14.4% operating margin, including $110M of tariff refunds.
Production and precision ag sales fell 6% to $3.998B, with operating margin of 13.2%.
Small ag and turf sales rose 12% to $3.383B with an 18.4% operating margin.
Construction and forestry sales rose 18% to $3.618B on 8 points of price, with a 12.1% operating margin.

keyMetrics.value: Four to five months on hand
keyMetrics.comparison: vs typical two to three months

guidance: Dan Pooley, Manager of Investor Communications, raised FY2026 net income to $4.75B-$5B and equipment operations cash flow to $5B-$5.5B.
Pooley guided PPA sales down about 10% (11%-12% margin), small ag and turf up about 15% (14.5%-15.5%) and C&F up about 20% (10.5%-11.5%).
Chris Seibert, Director of Investor Relations, cut FY2026 direct tariff expense to about $1.1B from $1.2B, assuming no further refunds.
Brent Norwood, CFO, expects Q4 PPA and C&F sales similar to Q3, with lower PPA and small ag margins on seasonal costs and no refund benefit.

qa.question: Is the net 2026 tariff impact a headwind, tailwind or neutral for 2027?
qa.answer: Norwood said about $1.1B of direct tariffs less $382M of refunds leaves roughly $750M net this year, and next year's run rate is closer to $1B, a step up.

qa.question: What lowered the tariff estimate to $1.1B, and how is the excavator launch going?
qa.answer: Seibert said Section 232 import rates fell from about 25% to 15% from June 1, covering five of 12 months and implying a 2027 tailwind; Brent Norwood, CFO, said three Deere-designed excavator models are shipping.

qa.question: Why does C&F price fall in Q4 after +8% in Q3, and how big could dealer rental become?
qa.answer: Seibert said Q3 lapped about 5% negative price a year earlier and full-year C&F price is 3 points; Brent Norwood, CFO, said 30%-35% of earthmoving transactions start as rentals but gave no size target.

qa.question: How does 2027 production versus retail set up, and what pricing should be expected?
qa.answer: Seibert said PPA and C&F are each underproducing retail by a couple of points this year; Deanna Kovar, President of Worldwide Agriculture & Turf, said pricing aims to cover inflation without a figure.

unanswered.question: Whether the 2028 European CAP policy change pulls 2027 demand forward, and a 2027 Europe forecast.
unanswered.how: Chris Seibert, Director of Investor Relations, said it is "too early to tell" and gave no forecast.

unanswered.question: Margin direction for next year and the $2B-$3B lifecycle parts opportunity after the FTC right-to-repair settlement.
unanswered.how: Seibert gave no margin direction and Brent Norwood, CFO, did not comment on the $2B-$3B figure.

guidanceRevisions: Net income: $4.5B-$5B to $4.75B-$5B; operating cash flow $4.5B-$5.5B to $5B-$5.5B.
PPA: sales down 5%-10% to down about 10%; margin 11%-13% to 11%-12%.
Industry: South America down about 15% to down 15%-20%; Europe flat to up 5% to about flat; earthmoving up about 5% to up 5%-10%.
Tariffs: direct expense about $1.2B to about $1.1B; net about $900M to about $750M.
whatChanged.toneShift: Last quarter Norwood said Deere's "baseline view remains" that 2026 is the ag cycle bottom; this quarter Kovar held that view but qualified it as "a measured recovery rather than a sharp rebound," and tariffs moved from a refund tailwind to a 2027 headwind.

risksMentioned: Brent Norwood, CFO, expects net tariff expense to step up to around $1B in 2027 from about $750M.
Chris Seibert, Director of Investor Relations, cited input and commodity volatility, Black Sea shipment disruptions and softness in the E.U. and Brazil.
Deanna Kovar, President of Worldwide Agriculture & Turf, said fertilizer price uncertainty has farmers looking for alternatives.
